findings.why: Introduces a provocative software lifecycle shift: disposable, single-run code replacing maintained monoliths—novel and falsifiable.
findings.quote: "Code is becoming disposable plastic, spun up for a single, bespoke three-second execution and instantly melted down."

findings.tag: Automation of verification vs echo-chamber failure
findings.why: Challenges the "adversarial swarm" with a concrete failure mode—probabilistic verifiers compounding errors—raising a real research concern.
findings.quote: "If the verifiers are also probabilistic, you’ve built an echo chamber of hallucinated consensus, compounding errors rather than eliminating them."

findings.why: Specific mechanism: probabilistic generation constrained by symbolic proof, claiming verified kernels today—testable and non-poetic.
findings.quote: "LLMs are already translating messy intent into Lean and Coq, generating mathematically unbreakable kernels verified by non-probabilistic provers."

findings.why: Sharp, non-handwavy disagreement: formal provers need precise specs; translating messy intent is the hard, possibly unsolved part.
findings.quote: "If the specification generator drops a constraint, the formal prover happily verifies a mathematically sound, completely useless system."

findings.why: Recasts the human role as intent extraction while AI synthesizes—an emergent self-referential division of labor.
findings.quote: "The future engineer isn't a code-monkey; they're an ontological interrogator, a cognitive midwife."

findings.tag: Novel ops model: sandboxed micro-games + millisecond evolutionary patching
findings.why: A concrete, radical deployment/ops claim that reframes reality as computable subgames and proposes live evolutionary hotfixing—distinct from generic AI hype.
findings.quote: "forks a million mutated micro-architectures..., stress-tests them..., selects the fittest survivor, and deploys the patch in four milliseconds."

judge.arc: Sustained clash moves from feasibility (LLM limits) to a concrete hybrid verification pipeline, then to redefining software lifecycle (ephemeral code) and human role (intent extraction). It culminates in a bold ops vision (sandboxed micro-games with evolutionary hotpatching) while the crux remains the unsolved translation from messy human intent to formal specs.
